transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Nice to meet you too. I came in because... well, for a long time now, I’ve just had this heavy, low feeling sitting on me most days. I mean, I’m still getting through my driving routes and my volunteer shifts just fine, but it’s like I’m just going through the motions instead of really being in my own life.
How long has this low feeling been present?
I'd say it's been going on for about three years now. It started right around the time my father died, and... well, it just hasn't really gone away since then.
Since your father died, have there been any stretches of two months or more when you felt essentially back to your usual self?
No, not really. I mean, there might be a good day here or there, but I can't remember any time where I felt totally normal for that long. It's just been pretty constant since he passed.
Do you often feel an intense longing or yearning for your father?
No, I wouldn't say that. I miss him, sure, but it's not like this intense yearning or anything. It's more just... he's gone, and things have felt kind of flat ever since.
During this period, have you often felt low in energy or tired?

Not really. I mean, I drive a truck for a living, so I get regular tired after a long shift. But I wouldn't say I've been unusually low on energy or dragging or anything like that. Just the normal amount of tired, I guess.
During these three years, have you often had trouble sleeping or slept much more than usual?

Yeah, I don't sleep too much, but I do have trouble getting a good night's rest. A lot of times, especially on nights before a run, I’ll just lie there thinking about the next day’s stops. Or I’ll wake up around four in the morning and just... not really get back to sleep. So even when I make it to work on time, I feel like I’m starting the day already worn down.
During these three years, have you often lost interest in or gotten much less pleasure from activities you usually enjoy?

No, I wouldn't say that. I still like doing the things I usually do. I mean, I'll still watch football on the weekends or tinker around in the garage, and I still enjoy it same as always. So, no, I haven't really lost interest in my normal stuff.
During this period, have you often felt hopeless about the future?

No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I don't really sit around feeling doomed or anything. I just take it one day at a time, you know? Get up, do my routes, pay the bills. The future is just... well, it's just out there. I don't feel hopeless about it.
Over the past three years, have you noticed any significant change in your appetite or weight?

No, not really. My appetite's been pretty much the same as it's always been. I eat my regular meals, grab a sandwich on the road... weight hasn't changed either, near as I can tell. My clothes still fit the same. So, no, nothing different there.
During these three years, have you often had trouble concentrating or making decisions?

Well, yeah, a little bit. I mean, I can still do my job fine, but... lately I catch myself having to reread delivery times. Or I'll just be staring at the schedule board longer than I really should be. It's just like my mind doesn't lock onto things the way it used to, you know? Just takes a bit more effort to focus on what I'm looking at.
During this period, have you often felt badly about yourself or like you were not good enough?

Yeah, I do. I guess... I keep comparing myself to the kind of man my dad was. Nobody is actually coming out and telling me I'm failing at anything, but I just hear it in my own head anyway. Just this thought that I should be further along in life by now, and that I ought to be handling things better than this.
